title: Katrina Kaif on Postpartum Skin, Beauty Standards and Feeling Her Best
excerpt: After facing trolling over her postpartum appearance, the actor says motherhood rebuilt her approach to skincare — and to what beauty means.
body:
• Katrina Kaif has spoken about how pregnancy changed her skin and her definition of beauty, saying postpartum sensitivity forced her to rebuild her skincare around soothing, restorative products.
  • Her comments follow a wave of social media trolling over her postpartum appearance after she attended a Ganpati celebration — her son Vihaan was born in November 2025.
  • Industry figures including Ali Fazal, Sonarika Bhadoria and Shivaleeka Oberoi condemned the remarks; Bhadoria called the scrutiny of new mothers "cruel."
  • "Looking my best is really about feeling my best, and that comes from taking care of myself as a whole," Kaif told The Hollywood Reporter India.

Katrina Kaif is pushing back on the internet's expectations of a new mother's body — with her own experience of it. The actor, who welcomed her son Vihaan with husband Vicky Kaushal in November 2025, has spoken about how pregnancy changed her skin and, more fundamentally, her understanding of beauty.

The comments come after a rare public appearance at a Ganpati celebration drew unsolicited scrutiny online, with users comparing her postpartum look to pre-pregnancy images. The discourse was met with significant backlash from industry colleagues. Ali Fazal, Sonarika Bhadoria and Shivaleeka Oberoi were among those who condemned the negative remarks.

Skin, sensitivity and self-care

In a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, Kaif described the physical recalibration that followed pregnancy. Her skin became markedly more sensitive, and finding products that worked took time. "Post-pregnancy, my skin became even more sensitive, so it was a really tricky time because I had to understand what products were working for me. I found myself looking for products that felt soothing, calming and restorative."

She tied the shift to a longer arc. Entering the industry through modelling and film, she encountered rigid stereotypes about how women were expected to look. Motherhood changed the frame: "When I started out early through my modelling and acting career, there were a lot of stereotypes about what the beauty standards were. Now for me, looking my best is really about feeling my best, and that comes from taking care of myself as a whole."

"Looking my best is really about feeling my best, and that comes from taking care of myself as a whole."

— Katrina Kaif, in The Hollywood Reporter India

An industry pushes back

The trolling around Kaif's appearance has become a wider conversation about postpartum body image. Television actor Sonarika Bhadoria — who became a mother herself in December 2025 — addressed the criticism directly on Instagram, arguing that a woman's body should not be treated as public property and that the expectation of an instant return to a pre-pregnancy appearance is unrealistic and cruel.

"A postpartum body is not a failed version of a woman's old body. It is evidence," Bhadoria wrote, in a post that extended beyond Kaif to every mother being judged while still healing. Shraddha Arya separately said women should not be viewed as "before and after" pictures, and NDTV examined why postpartum recovery does not follow one fixed timeline — pointing to the compounded effects of hormones, sleep deprivation and recovery.

The wellness shift

Kaif's own regimen now centres on the unglamorous fundamentals: eating well, staying active, meditation, managing inflammation — and time away from her phone. It is a long way from the aesthetic demands of her early career, and it lands at a moment when the conversation about celebrity bodies is shifting from admiration to accountability.

For Kaif, who has spent two decades as one of Bollywood's most scrutinised faces, the message is simple and hard-won: the standard is feeling well, not looking untouched.
